q: Should a steel plant buying Jharia coking coal count mine methane in Scope 3?
title: Jharia coking coal: mine methane in Scope 3
short: Yes, if you report category 1 for coal. Methane escapes from the seam during mining, and deep coking coal seams release more than surface mines. Without mine data, IPCC Tier 1 gives 18 cubic metres of methane per tonne for underground mining, a default with a wide range.
audience: Steel plants and coke makers buying coking coal from Jharia and other Jharkhand mines

ul: Underground mining: 10 to 25 cubic metres per tonne, 18 average (IPCC 2006).
Post mining handling: about 2.5 cubic metres per tonne more.
One cubic metre of methane weighs about 0.67 kg.

p: Ask the supplier which mines the coal comes from and whether they measure ventilation methane. Mixed underground and opencast supply needs a weighted figure.
Mine methane is upstream of your plant, so it is Scope 3 for you. It is not part of the CBAM figure for steel.
